_comment: Accepted `npm audit` findings (operations plan, Task E8). CI fails on any high or
critical advisory that is not listed here. An entry needs the package, the advisory id
(a GHSA id, or the name of the vulnerable dependency the package inherits it from), why
the product is not exposed, and the date it was last read. `.github/scripts/npm-audit-gate.mjs`
reads this file; it also prints entries that no longer match anything, which is the

advisories.reason: Wasp's server SDK pulls nodemailer for the email sender. The exposure is the message-level `raw` option, which lets a caller read a local file or drive an SSRF through the delivered message; the portal only ever sends Wasp's own templated verification, password-reset and invitation emails, and nothing in portal/src constructs `raw`. A non-breaking bump exists, but portal/package-lock.json is regenerated by the Wasp toolchain, so it belongs to a portal task rather than to this one.

Reached only through nodemon inside `.wasp/out/server`, the generated development server. It is a build-time dependency of a generated tree that is gitignored and never deployed: the portal container images run `wasp build` output, not nodemon. A regular-expression denial of service in a version checker on a developer's machine is not a production exposure.
The same nodemon chain as GHSA-c2qf-rxjj-qqgw; this row is the intermediate package. The only fix npm offers is nodemon 3.x, which Wasp 0.25 pins for its own generated server.

The same nodemon chain as GHSA-c2qf-rxjj-qqgw; this row is the top of it. Wasp 0.25 pins nodemon 2.x in the generated development server, so upgrading it here would be undone by the next `wasp build`.
